## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** one documentation issue remains in the Live tests section; at `a1dc829` all three items from the [previous review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13024#issuecomment-5855258259) are resolved, as the [reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13024#issuecomment-5879378353) states.

### Live tests: after-state provenance is unclear

The description says `iw phy` showed `SAE_OFFLOAD` after the fix on both the MacBookPro15,2 and 16,1. The reply says the MacBookPro15,2 after-state was "not captured" and is "still inferred". The quoted `iw` lines (`ABSENT`/`present`, "SAE authentication offload") also do not match what `iw` prints. **Impact:** documentation only, but it is the PR's only after-state evidence.

**Suggested change:** state which results were measured on which machine, mark the rest as expected, and paste literal output or name the command used.

<details><summary>Evidence (source reading and text comparison, not a hardware run)</summary>

# Live tests: after-state provenance and iw transcripts (documentation note)

Kind: source reading plus a text comparison of the PR description and the author's reply. Not a runtime reproduction; no Apple or Broadcom hardware was used.

## The two statements

PR description (current text):

> **After**, on BCM4364 (`MacBookPro16,1` and `MacBookPro15,2`):
> - `iw phy` advertises `* [ SAE_OFFLOAD ]: SAE authentication offload`.
>
> The after-state above was captured on separate reboots of two machines; the "before" state reported here is the same firmware revision.

Author reply, hardware section (edited 2026-09-30):

> ## After state: not captured
> ... The claim "SAE_OFFLOAD returns once the block is gone" is therefore still inferred from the source above, not measured.

## What iw actually prints

iw prints only the extended features that are present, one line each, in the form `* [ NAME ]: description`. It never prints an ABSENT marker, and the SAE_OFFLOAD description has been `SAE offload support` since the feature was added to iw in 2019.

```
$ git clone https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/jberg/iw.git && cd iw
$ git log -1 --format=%h
e86c546
$ grep -n 'ext_feat_case(SAE_OFFLOAD' info.c
143:	ext_feat_case(SAE_OFFLOAD, "SAE offload support");
157:	ext_feat_case(SAE_OFFLOAD_AP, "AP mode SAE authentication offload support");
$ git log -p -G'SAE_OFFLOAD, "' --format='commit %h %ad' --date=short -- info.c | grep -E '^commit|^[+-].*SAE_OFFLOAD, "'
commit 0976378 2022-05-27
+	ext_feat_case(SAE_OFFLOAD, "SAE offload support");
-		ext_feat_print(tb, SAE_OFFLOAD, "SAE offload support");
commit b5c0c33 2019-08-05
+		ext_feat_print(tb, SAE_OFFLOAD, "SAE offload support");
$ sed -n '864,870p' info.c
		printf("\tSupported extended features:\n");

		for (feat = 0; feat < NUM_NL80211_EXT_FEATURES; feat++) {
			if (!ext_feature_isset(nla_data(tb), nla_len(tb), feat))
				continue;
			ext_feat_print(feat);
		}
$ git grep -n -i -w 'absent' -- '*.c' | wc -l
0
```

So `iw phy phy0 info | grep -E 'SAE_OFFLOAD|4WAY_HANDSHAKE'` on a phy with only `4WAY_HANDSHAKE_AP_PSK` set prints one `* [ 4WAY_HANDSHAKE_AP_PSK ]: AP mode PSK offload support` line, not the four ABSENT/present lines shown under "Mechanism, verified on the affected hardware". The After line's `SAE authentication offload` text is not what iw prints for SAE_OFFLOAD.

## Related public evidence

Issue #9802 reports a measured after-state on a `MacBookPro16,1` (BCM4364B3, firmware `9.30.514.0.32.5.94`): reloading brcmfmac with `feature_disable=0` exposed `SAE_OFFLOAD` and a WPA3-only network connected. The MacBookPro15,2 in this PR runs firmware `9.30.503.0.32.5.92`.
</details>

<details><summary>Details: Verified, small corrections, related PRs</summary>

**Verified:**
- hostap `41638606` is in `hostap_2_12` and `main`; Arch's revert first ships in `2:2.12-1` (built 2026-08-10), which the Omarchy mirrors serve. brcmfmac reports port authorization only on 802.1X fast-transition roams (v7.2, 7.2.8, mainline).
- Both suites pass at `a1dc829` (20 and 12 assertions) and on a local merge with `quattro` `8b4eae6`. Deleting the T2 check from each gate now fails the suite that owns it (table below).
- The new `1786391100.sh` sentence matches both gates.
- The Related open PRs section describes #10306 (`5a5d5b1`) and #9803 (`7f04107`) accurately.
- `1790165000.sh` is unchanged since the previous review.

**Small corrections (optional):**
- The Arch patch sits at the packaging repository root, not under `patches/` (installer comment and description).
- Description: `BRCMF_FEAT_SAE_EXT`'s second reference is the firmware capability map (`brcmf_fwcap_map`), and `cyw/core.c` does have a user-space SAE (`external_auth`) path. The Apple parts use the WCC ops, which have none, so the conclusion holds for these Macs.

**Related open PRs:** #11259 and #13362 also edit the installer leaf and conflict textually with this PR's `fix-brcmfmac-supplicant.sh`. #11259 also conflicts in `1786391100.sh`, where both narrowed gates would need rewriting with its sysfs helper; the new T2 test cases merge unchanged.

# T2 gate deletions against both suites (verification of the earlier optional test item, not a finding)

Kind: isolated command-only run with the suites' own stubbed `lspci`, `sudo` and `omarchy-state`. Run from a checkout of the PR; writes only under `mktemp -d`.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Deletes the 106b:180[12] (T2) check from each of the three gates in a
# throwaway copy of the repository and runs both brcmfmac suites against it.
# Usage: bash verify-t2-gates.sh [repo-root]   (writes only under mktemp -d)
set -uo pipefail

root=$(cd -- "${1:-.}" && pwd)
work=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT

suites=(brcmfmac-supplicant-test.sh brcmfmac-wpa3-cleanup-test.sh)

run_suites() {
  local label=$1 dir=$2 suite out status
  for suite in "${suites[@]}"; do
    out=$(bash "$dir/test/shell.d/$suite" 2>&1)
    status=$?
    if (( status == 0 )); then
      printf '%-22s %-32s passes (%s ok)\n' "$label" "$suite" "$(grep -c '^ok - ' <<<"$out")"
    else
      printf '%-22s %-32s FAILS: %s\n' "$label" "$suite" \
        "$(grep '^not ok - ' <<<"$out" | tail -n 1 | sed 's/^not ok - //')"
    fi
  done
}

copy() {
  local dest="$work/$1"
  mkdir -p "$dest/test"
  cp -r "$root/install" "$root/migrations" "$dest/"
  cp -r "$root/test/shell.d" "$dest/test/"
  printf '%s\n' "$dest"
}

run_suites unmodified "$root"

d=$(copy installer)
sed -i '/^  ! lspci -nn | grep "106b:180\[12\]" >\/dev\/null &&$/d' \
  "$d/install/hardware/apple/fix-brcmfmac-supplicant.sh"
! grep -q '106b:180' "$d/install/hardware/apple/fix-brcmfmac-supplicant.sh" || { echo "installer mutation not applied"; exit 2; }
run_suites "no T2 in installer" "$d"

d=$(copy legacy)
sed -i -e '/^if lspci -nn | grep "106b:180\[12\]" >\/dev\/null ||$/d' \
  -e 's/^  ! { \[\[ \$sys_vendor == Apple\* \]\] &&$/if ! { [[ $sys_vendor == Apple* ]] \&\&/' \
  "$d/migrations/1786391100.sh"
! grep -q '106b:180' "$d/migrations/1786391100.sh" || { echo "legacy mutation not applied"; exit 2; }
bash -n "$d/migrations/1786391100.sh" || { echo "legacy mutation broke syntax"; exit 2; }
run_suites "no T2 in 1786391100" "$d"

d=$(copy cleanup)
sed -i 's/grep -E "106b:180\[12\]|14e4:(4464|4425|4433)"/grep -E "14e4:(4464|4425|4433)"/' \
  "$d/migrations/1790165000.sh"
! grep -q 'grep -E "106b:180' "$d/migrations/1790165000.sh" || { echo "cleanup mutation not applied"; exit 2; }
run_suites "no T2 in 1790165000" "$d"
```
